findings.title: Phone (touch): the bench can't be finished. The sign-off button and the 47/220 Ω bins are off-screen in portrait, and the HUD covers them in landscape
findings.problem:
On a phone the bench is touch-only: there are no on-screen buttons for P, F, X, A/S/D or Enter. The only input is tapping the 3D parts.

Portrait, 390×844:
- The bench camera pulls back by `clamp(1.25/aspect,1,2.1)` (src/game.ts:371). At aspect 0.46 that clamps to 2.1, which still isn't wide enough for the 4.3 m bench.
- The left column of bins (47 Ω, 220 Ω) is completely off the left edge. Only a few pixels of the 100 Ω and 470 Ω bins show.
- The sign-off stamp (POWERAT.x+.52, station.ts:209) is off the right edge.
- I made a passing setup (soakDone true), then tapped a 6 px grid over the right edge (x 330–389, y 470–530). The station index stayed 0, so the cabinet can't be signed off.
- The prompt pill reads "Enter Sign off", but a phone has no Enter key and the pill isn't tappable.
- The bench fills only the middle sixth of the screen; the lower half is empty pink rug.
- The Rhythm pad's elegant fix needs two 47 Ω blocks, which can't be reached at all.

Landscape, 844×390:
- The station panel covers the power lever, the ACROSS slot and the sign-off stamp.
- The objective card covers the 47 and 100 Ω bins.
- The panel has pointer-events:none (src/ui/ui.css:218), so blind taps may land, but the controls can't be seen.

A phone player who reaches the bench can't complete the job. A12 (phone bench layout) was OPEN in R3B; it now blocks play.
findings.fix:
1. Add a portrait bench layout in src/stations/arcade/station.ts:
   - When `game.view.camera.aspect<0.8`, move `this.top`'s contents into a 2-row layout: bins in a 2×2 block above the board (`BINSAT={x:-.5,z:-.9}`), and the power lever plus sign-off stamp below the board (`POWERAT={x:.6,z:.75}`).
   - Alternatively, give the station a `view` per aspect (`view.distance` about 7.5, `lookX` 0) and scale `this.top` by 0.75 on the x axis.
2. Add a touch action strip at the bench (src/ui/objectives.ts, next to `.bench-chip`) with 4 large buttons: POWER, FLIP, SIGN OFF ✓, STAND UP. Make the prompt pill tappable: it calls `station.key(<code>)` for its key.
3. In landscape, hide `.station-panel` rows while `body[data-bench]` is set and the viewport height is under 500 px, or dock the panel to the bottom-left at 50 % width.
findings.verify: Rerun mockups/review5/tools/arcade-play/s9b-phonesign.mjs at 390×844 and 844×390. Tapping the visible ✓ must make `station.index` 1. Add a Playwright spec `arcade: phone portrait can finish a cabinet by taps only` (viewport 390×844, no keyboard; use page.mouse.click on the projected screen positions of the bins, pads, lever and stamp). Retake shots 82/85: every bin, the lever and the stamp sit inside the viewport and outside every HUD rect.
findings.verify_reason: The layout problem is real, but the claim that the bench can't be finished is wrong. In portrait (390×844) the 47 Ω and 220 Ω bins are fully off the left edge. Only about 4×24 px of the ✓ stamp's dark rim shows at x 386–390 (my crop). The 'Enter Sign off' pill has pointer-events:none (ui.css:208). Even so, I tapped (389,490) in the passed state and station.index went 0→1, so the cabinet signed off. The reviewer's grid ran x=330,336…384 and never reached x≥386. Its first taps could also land on the POWER box and reset soakDone. In landscape (844×390) the panel (x530–820, y96–299) covers the lever and stamp, but it has pointer-events:none. A blind tap at (636,262) signed off (index 1). The room can be finished in portrait: pinball 470‖470 = 12.7 mA ★, rhythm flipped with its starting 47 Ω = 6.25 mA 'Works' tier 1, claw/handheld/hopper 470+470. Rhythm's ★ answer (47‖47) can't be built, so the ★ bonus is lost on phones. A 4 px sliver at the screen edge, where OS edge gestures live, is close to unusable, so this is a serious P1 phone issue but not a strict block.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-play/v1-phone.mjs log: 'phoneP signed by tap at 389 490', index after taps 1
mockups/review5/shots/verify-arcade-play-03-portrait-stamp-sliver-crop.jpg (stamp rim only ~4 px wide at the right edge)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-arcade-play-02-landscape-hud-hidden.jpg (HUD hidden: lever at ~570,215, stamp at ~636,262, both under the panel rect 530–820×96–299)
findings.fix_correction: Keep the reviewer's layout fix (portrait bench layout or wider pull-back, and a touch action strip). Also correct the evidence: the stamp is reachable but only as a ~4 px sliver at x≈389, and landscape sign-off works through the panel blind. The test must check that every bin, the lever and the stamp project fully inside the viewport with at least 44×44 px tap targets, not merely that a tap somewhere works. Clamping only to 2.1 in game.ts:372 isn't enough at aspect 0.46. Either raise the clamp to about 2.8 for aspect<0.6, or lay the bench out in two rows. Making the prompt pill tappable (pointer-events:auto, calling station.key(p.key) for single-key prompts) is the cheapest partial fix.

findings.title: The P key toggles. Pressing P while the prompt says "P Fuse cooling" or "P Play test" switches the bench OFF, so the natural retry kills the run
findings.problem:
POWER is a toggle (station.ts:268-270), but the prompt describes a state, not the action:
- While tripped it shows "P Fuse cooling" (station.ts:483).
- While the kid plays it shows "P Play test" (station.ts:484).

This is the exact DR-19 case. I played it with real keys: P (trip) → X, 3, A (fix the chain while the fuse cools) → P, the instinctive "try again".
- Result: `powered:false`. Three seconds later the meter reads POWER OFF and nothing happens. The player has to press P a second time.
- Pressing P during the play test (the prompt literally says "P Play test") powers off and resets the soak to 0 (s5 log: soak 1.5 → 0, powered false).

A new player gets punished for following the prompt, and loses the 3 s play test. It feels like the bench is broken.
findings.fix:
In src/stations/arcade/station.ts:
1. In `prompt()`, always describe what P will do:
   - tripped: `{key:'P',text:'Power off'}`, or better, no P prompt at all and a non-key status chip "Fuse cooling 2.1 s";
   - soaking: `{key:'P',text:'Power off (stops the play test)'}`;
   - otherwise 'Power on' or 'Power off'.
2. Make P after a chain change while tripped mean "keep power on": in `act('power')`, if `this.tripped && this.powered`, ignore the press (play the `hm` voice) instead of powering off. The PTC conducts again by itself once cool, so the fix goes live without another press. Alternatively, turn power off only on a long press or a second press within 0.4 s.
3. Make the lever show its state: the lever already rotates (station.ts:332). Add an ON/OFF plate (`sign(p,'ON',…)`) that swaps text.
findings.verify: Add a test to tests/station-arcade.spec.ts: power → trip → `slot across` → place 220 → press KeyP → wait 3 s. Expect `station.live===true` and `soakDone` true after 3.2 s more. Also: press KeyP mid-soak only when the prompt says 'Power off'. Retake shot 52 showing PLAY TEST running.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced this with real keys. KeyP tripped the fuse and the prompt read 'P Fuse cooling'. I then pressed X, 3, A (chain fixed while cooling) and KeyP again: powered went false. Three seconds later: live false, prompt 'P Power on', meter POWER OFF. Next I powered on and waited 1.5 s (soak 1.5, prompt 'P Play test'). Pressing KeyP gave powered false and soak 0. The code toggles at station.ts:268-270, and the prompts at :483-484 describe a state, not what P does. This is the exact DR-19 check case.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-play/v2-keys.mjs log: 'after retry P {p:false,…trip:true}', '3s later {p:false,live:false}', 'P during play test {p:false,soak:0}'

findings.title: Pressing R at the bench reloads the level at once and wipes every signed-off cabinet
findings.problem:
At the bench the station only claims its own 12 keys (station.ts:352-354). Every other key falls through to the walking handler (game.ts:164-166).
- KeyR maps to `action('restart')`, which is `location.reload()` (game.ts:178), with no confirm, during play.
- At the bench the player's left hand sits on A S D X F P, and E or Esc stands up. R is right next to E and F.
- s4: pressing R while seated gave `time 0`, `trayReady false`, `atBench false`: every signed-off cabinet is lost.

With 12 bench keys plus E/Esc, a stray R is likely, and the cost is the whole room. This breaks DR-22 (no game key acts destructively at a menu-like station) and the forgiving-interaction spirit of AGENTS 7.
findings.fix:
1. In src/game.ts:164, while `this.atBench`, swallow every key the station doesn't claim (return after `station.key`). Tab, R, Space and Q must not act at a bench.
2. Make restart a hold (KeyR for 0.8 s with a ring fill on the pause button), or put a confirm on the pause menu, so a stray R is never destructive anywhere.
findings.verify: Add a test: enter the bench, sign off cabinet 1, press KeyR. Expect `snapshot().station.served.length===1` and `time>0`. Retake shot 54 showing the bench still up.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. I signed off cabinet 1 (served 1, index 1, still at the bench) and pressed KeyR. The page navigated ('R -> reloaded'), and the snapshot after reload read time 0, served 0, atBench false. Code: game.ts:164 only returns early for keys the station claims or E/Esc. Every other key falls through to game.ts:166, where KeyR calls action('restart') → location.reload() at game.ts:178, with no confirm.

findings.title: The payoff is off-camera: the play-test kid, the cabinet's TILT marquee and lamp, and the back-wall cabinets lighting up are never in the bench view, and the bench camera can't be orbited
findings.problem:
The design's feedback loop is:
- "a kid plays each cabinet for 3 s" and hops, cheers or slumps;
- the serviced cabinet's marquee flashes TILT! on a trip;
- its lamp glows in the LED colour;
- the five broken cabinets on the back wall light up as each one is signed off.

None of this is in the bench frame:
- The serviced cabinet and kid stand at `t.x+OX-2.75`, about x −2.95 (station.ts:215). The bench camera (distance 5.9, pitch 0.98, FOV 30) frames about x −2.7…2.3. Only a sliver of the kid's hair and one arm shows at the left edge (crop of shot 22).
- `room.light()` fires on the back wall, behind and above the monitor, also out of frame.
- The bench camera ignores right-drag: yaw snaps back to `want` every frame (game.ts:372), and wheel zoom is disabled at the bench (game.ts:175). Shot 92, after orbit(−400): identical framing.

So during the 3 s play test the player stares at a purple progress bar. On sign-off they get a toast and a bell. The only laugh R4B found (TILT) is now invisible.

From the room camera (standing up mid-test, shots 40/41) the kid is a tiny shape hidden behind the bench head and marker. It is still a realistic human child (orange shirt, skin-tone sphere head, brown hair: station.ts:225-231), which breaks DR-60's blob-only cast.

For a Good Job-style game the success beat is the reward. Here it happens off-screen five times.
findings.fix:
1. Bring the play test into frame:
   - Move the serviced cabinet to the bench's back-left corner, facing the camera: `group(root,t.x+OX-1.55,0,t.z-1.25,0)`, 0.8× scale. Its screen and marquee then sit above the bins, in frame.
   - Or add a picture-in-picture: render a 320×200 inset from a second camera aimed at the kid while `soak>0`.
   - Stand the kid (as a small blob with a cap, `blob()` from render/actors, not a human) on a step between the cabinet and the bench, at about x −1.9.
2. While soaking, have the cabinet screen animate (scrolling `hot()` colours) and play chiptune blips.
3. On sign-off, do a 1.2 s camera beat:
   - lerp `view.lookX` toward the back-wall cabinet that just lit (room.ts:122) with a 0.15 s hitstop, then return;
   - or set `this.game.focus` to `m.at` for 1 s.
4. Allow ±0.6 rad of bench yaw from right-drag (keep `want` as the rest yaw, spring back after release) so players can look left.
findings.verify: Retake the bench shots during the soak and right after sign-off (`arcade-play-22`, `-24` equivalents). The kid, the cabinet screen and the TILT marquee are all inside the frame, and the lit back cabinet is in frame within 1.2 s of Enter. Grep: no '#f2c49b' in src/stations/arcade.
findings.verify_reason: At 1440×900 the bench frame never shows the serviced cabinet's screen, marquee or kid, or the back wall. The top of the frame is floor behind the bench, and the left edge shows only a sliver of the cabinet and kid (my shots 04/05/06; the reviewer's crop-22). Back-wall cabinets sit at z −6.9 (room.ts:82), and room.light() adds its glow and confetti there (room.ts:122-123), outside the bench camera's view. The bench camera ignores pitch input (it uses v.pitch) and pulls yaw back to `want` every frame (game.ts:372; instantly in ?manual, within about 0.25 s live). Wheel zoom returns early at the bench (game.ts:175). The kid is a realistic human: a skin-tone #f2c49b sphere head, brown hair and an orange shirt (station.ts:229-231). It is clearly visible as a small human in the room view (my shot 08), which breaks DR-60. One extra detail: in landscape 844×390 (aspect 2.16) the cabinet does come into frame at the left (my shot 02), so how bad this is depends on aspect.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-arcade-play-05-space-at-bench.jpg and -06-tab-at-bench.png (play test passed, no cabinet, kid or back wall in frame)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-arcade-play-08-card-after-sitting-without-tray.jpg (human kid with skin-tone head next to the bench's left end)
findings.fix_correction: The fix is sound. One check: if the serviced cabinet moves to about (t.x+OX−1.55, t.z−1.25), its fixed collider at station.ts:224 and the kid's at :232 must move with it, and it must not overlap the back-row bins (world x≈−1.7, z≈−2.5) in the bench frame. Verify by retaking the bench shot.

findings.title: The prompts invite mistakes: "P Power on" on cabinets that start broken, so looking first costs 3–5 mistakes against a 2-damage limit (A7 still open)
findings.verify: Spec run: power each untouched start, then fix. Final `station.mistakes===0` and `trips===0`, and the third bonus stays lit. A deliberately wrong edit (pinball: put a 47 Ω block in the chain) still counts 1.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in code and in a run. prompt() returns 'P Power on' whenever the chain holds a block (station.ts:485). After cabinet 1 my prompt read 'P Power on' (v2 log 'signed … prompt: P Power on'). Pressing power on the untouched rhythm start (reversed LED) counted mistakes 0→1 after 0.6 s (v3 log 'rhythm diagnose power … mis:1'). By the logic, claw 220 Ω on 12 V gives 44.8 mA: a fault, then a block pop at about 1.7 s, so +2 mistakes and +1 credit. Handheld 220 Ω on 9 V gives 31.7 mA: +1. I lowered the priority because AGENTS 6 makes the overall grade the best of three axes. These mistakes only lower the damage axis on the card. They never cost the 'fuse tripped' bonus, since none of those three starts trips. So it hurts the messaging (the UI invites a punished action), not the outcome.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-play/v3-brute.mjs log: 'rhythm diagnose power {p:true,…mis:1}' with prompt 'P Power off'

findings.title: Brute force is free: the meter shows the live current at once, swaps under 0.6 s are never counted, and blocks are billed only at sign-off
findings.problem:
With power on I swapped 47 → 100 → 220 → 470 in position A, about 0.3 s each (s5).
- The meter and panel showed 62.5, 29.7, 13.6 and 6.4 mA, the first two over the LED's rating.
- `mistakes` stayed 1 and `trips` stayed 1. Only the parallel pair that tripped the fuse counted.

Why it's free:
- An over-rating or dim setup is only explained and counted after `runT>.6` (station.ts:390).
- Credits are billed from the final setup at sign-off (`served.push({cost:v.cost})`, station.ts:273), plus popped parts.
- So cycling the bins while watching the LIGHT bar, with its ★ zone painted on (drawMeter, station.ts:561), finds the elegant answer without the formula, at no cost in credits or grade.

R4B's "step until the bar turns green" is still the dominant strategy. DR-38 (tiers reward understanding; brute force costs credits) fails.
findings.fix:
Pick one, in src/stations/arcade/station.ts:

(a) Predict-then-test:
- While powered, blocks can't be placed. `slot` with `this.powered` returns false, with the toast-free `hm` voice and the lever wobbling.
- So every try is power off → change → power on.
- Count a try each time power goes on with a failing setup, at any duration: move `fault(false)` to the power-on edge when `judge().tier===0`.

(b) Bill each block taken from a bin:
- `spent+=BLOCK_COST*0.5` on `pick` when the block is placed and later removed;
- show the running spend on the panel's Parts row.

Keep the live meter, but show the ★ zone only after the first passing play test.
findings.verify: Script the s5 brute-force loop and expect `mistakes` to rise by 2 or more (option a) or `spent` by 2 or more (option b). Existing clean specs still pass with ★ on every cabinet.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. With power on, I swapped position A every 0.3 s through 47, 100, 220, 470, 220, 100, 47, 100, 220 (62.5, 29.7, 13.6, 6.4 mA…). mistakes stayed 0, trips 0 and spent 0. The final 220 passed ★ (tier 3), and sign-off billed only 1 credit. The 0.6 s runT gate (station.ts:390) and the 0.5 s ledT gate (:386) both reset in changed() (:247). Billing comes from the final setup at sign-off (:273). This fails DR-38 directly.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-play/v3-brute.mjs log: 8× 'before swap … mis:0, trips:0, spent:0', then 'final … tier:3', 'signed … spent:1'
findings.fix_correction: Prefer option (b), billing per placed-then-removed block. Option (a) reverses the stated design that 'the circuit is live: every change shows on the meter at once' (station.ts:6). It also breaks the existing spec step at tests/station-arcade.spec.ts:74, which swaps blocks while live; that spec would need rewriting.

findings.title: No cable, no chaos route, no physical bonus: the 22×16 m hall is a corridor to a menu, and throwing the tray at the bench doesn't count
findings.problem:
Everything the job needs happens on the bench keypad. The room contributes one carry of about 18 m (spawn → storeroom → bench, about 8 s at sprint in s1).

No cable:
- `rope.maxLength` is 10 but the cable is neither simulated nor drawn in station rooms (game.ts:104, :92). DR-05 fails.
- The action bar still shows the F plug button and the Q slingshot button (shots 01, 10). F only shrugs. These are false affordances.

No chaos route:
- The level has `obstacles:[]` and no designed shortcut (src/levels/arcade.ts:26). DR-01 fails.
- Throwing the tray (Q) at the bench from 1.9 m didn't deliver it. It flew over the bench to z −5.1/−6.1, and I had to walk round the right end to fetch it (s4, s10).
- `dropped()` is only called from the E drop path (game.ts:210); a throw never calls it.

No physical bonus:
- All three bonuses are bench metrics (station.ts:118-121). DR-10 fails.

The 132 props are scenery to push through on the way. Compared with the Playground pins or the Meeting glass, this room has no moment a player would want to show a friend.
findings.fix:
1. Chaos delivery: call `this.station?.dropped?.(p)` for a thrown prop when it comes to rest. In `Game.step`, track the thrown prop, and once its speed is under 0.3 m/s call `station.dropped`. Widen the arcade test to accept a tray resting on or within 1.2 m of the bench top (`q.y>.9 && |q.x−t.x|<2.3 && |q.z−t.z|<.9`). Add a 'basket!' cheer and a bonus: "Deliver the tray by throwing it".
2. Give the room one physical cable act. Each signed-off cabinet must be re-plugged with a short room cable from a floor strip at the back wall (the existing reel prop at (−7.6,6.2) becomes the job reel), or drag the serviced cabinet's lead to its back-wall spot. Either way the strain colours and slingshot reach the room. Alternatively hide F and Q on the action bar in station rooms (src/ui) so there is no false affordance.
3. Add one chaos bonus target: knock the prize-shelf balls (room.ts:105) off with a thrown block, or bowl the cones (`cones` recipe) like the Playground pins.
findings.verify: New spec 'arcade: throwing the tray onto the bench delivers it' (walk to (0.4,0.3), Q, advance 2 → `trayReady` true). A survey shot shows the chaos target. `snapshot().rope.maxLength>0` and the cable is visible, or the action bar hides F/Q at `level.station`.
findings.verify_reason: I checked the code and a run. simulateCable/drawCable run only when !station (game.ts:104), and the anchor, plug and socket are hidden in station rooms (game.ts:92), so there is no cable act (DR-05). The level has obstacles:[] (arcade.ts:26). Throwing (game.ts:183) never calls station.dropped, which only runs from the E drop path (game.ts:210). In my run, throwing the tray from (0.4,0.3) sent it to (4.09,0.87,−3.37): trayReady stayed false, damage went 0→1 and cost +10. All three bonuses are bench metrics (station.ts:118-121). In the room view the F (plug) action button shows enabled when Pip isn't carrying anything (my shot 08, reviewer shot 08), so it is a false affordance.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-play/v4-flow.mjs log: '#6 thrown tray pos {x:4.09,y:0.87,z:-3.37} trayReady false damage 0 -> 1 cost 10'

findings.title: Cabinets 3, 4 and 5 all have the same answer (470 + 470 Ω): two of five puzzles are repeats
findings.problem:
`best()` for the Claw (12 V green, ★ 10–13.3 mA), the Handheld (9 V red, ★ 5–8.3 mA) and the Coin hopper (5 V base, ★ 4–6 mA) is the same chain: 470 + 470 = 940 Ω.
- Claw: 10.5 mA. Handheld: 7.44 mA. Hopper: 4.57 mA. All tier 3 in s2 and s3.
- The spec says so itself: "the same chain keeps it in the ★ zone" (tests/station-arcade.spec.ts:47-52).

After the Claw, a player who found 940 Ω just rebuilds it twice. The battery-life idea and the base-resistor idea are explained in text but never change what the player has to do. The last 40 % of the room is rote, and DR-27 (each job adds an idea the player must act on) fails for jobs 4 and 5.
findings.fix:
Retune src/stations/arcade/logic.ts JOBS so each best() answer differs and needs the new idea:
- Handheld: band [.003,.008] → ★ 3–4.7 mA. Then 470+470+470 (1410 Ω, 4.96 mA → retune) or a 3-block chain is needed, and the battery-life line visibly changes (about 100 h vs 67 h).
- Hopper: band [.0025,.006], or base 3.3 V. The answer becomes a single 470 Ω (5.7 mA) or 470+220. The new idea is "enough current to saturate, not maximal".

Add a unit test in src/stations/arcade/logic.test.ts asserting the five `best(j)` chains are pairwise different.
findings.verify: `npm.cmd test` with the new logic.test.ts case. Rerun the s2 solve script with the updated chains; all five tier 3 with different chains.
findings.verify_reason: I checked the math against logic.ts:62-83 and best() (logic.ts:185-190). Claw: 9.9 V/941 = 10.5 mA, ★ 10–13.3. Handheld: 7/941 = 7.44 mA, ★ 5–8.33. Hopper: 4.3/941 = 4.57 mA, ★ 4–6. In each case one block misses the ★ zone and 470+470 is the fewest-block answer. The spec says so itself (station-arcade.spec.ts:49-54). However, the reviewer's fix numbers are wrong. Handheld band [.003,.008] gives ★ 3–4.67 mA, but 1410 Ω gives 4.96 mA, so no chain reaches tier 3 and best() returns undefined. Hopper: a single 470 Ω on the 5 V pin gives 9.1 mA, not 5.7.
extra_evidence: src/stations/arcade/logic.ts:185-190 (best: fewest blocks, ties least current)
findings.fix_correction:
Use bands that give distinct, valid answers:
- Handheld: band [.003,.009] → ★ 3–5 mA. 470+470+470 = 1410 Ω gives 4.96 mA ★. No 1- or 2-block chain works: 940 Ω gives 7.4 mA, above ★. Battery about 101 h vs 67 h. Update the spec line 51 expectation (67 → ~101).
- Hopper: band [.006,.012] → ★ 6–8 mA. Fewest blocks with least current is 470+220 = 690 Ω → 6.22 mA, which still exceeds the motor's 2 mA and stays under the 20 mA pin limit.
Add the pairwise-distinct best(j) assertion in a logic unit test, and update tests/station-arcade.spec.ts:50-55 to the new chains.

findings.title: While Pip carries the tray, the yellow marker hovers over the tray in Pip's hands, not over the bench he must take it to
findings.problem:
Step 1's marker target is `at:()=>this.tray?.body.translation()` (station.ts:109), so the arrow always sits above the tray.
- Before pickup that is right.
- Once Pip holds it, the bouncing cone floats over his own hands (shots 09, 10). Nothing in the world says where the tray goes.
- The card says "…to the service bench", but the bench is just one of many counters in a busy room, and the prompt only changes to "Set the tray on the bench" within 2.4 m.

DR-42 and DR-44 say the marker points at the current step's target. During a carry the target is the destination.
findings.fix: In src/stations/arcade/station.ts:109, set `at:()=>this.game.held?.spec.id==='blocks'?{x:this.table.x+BINSAT.x+OX,z:this.table.z+BINSAT.z}:(this.tray?.body.translation()??this.stand)`. Also add a drop-zone cue while carrying: a pulsing ring decal on the bench top where the bins appear (reuse `game.burst(...,'ring')` every 1 s, or a flat ring mesh shown while held).
findings.verify: Retake shot 10 while carrying. The cone is over the bench's bin corner and a ring shows on the bench top. tests/station-arcade.spec.ts still passes.
findings.verify_reason: Step 1's at() is always the tray's translation (station.ts:109). objectives.ts:117-118 sets the marker at (at.x, 2.1, at.z) whenever not at the bench, so during the carry the cone bobs over Pip's own hands. I saw this in shot 10 (the cone sits above Pip and the tray, and nothing marks the bench). DR-42 applies.

findings.title: The bench shows about 100 words, and every key value three times (REGRESSION check of DR-40/41: still failing)
findings.problem:
Counted during the pinball trip (s12), HUD text only:
- card: 7 words;
- station panel: 31 (spec, story sentence, Chain/Current/Parts rows);
- toast: 19;
- prompt: 3;
- stand-up chip: 3.

That is 63 words. The monitor adds about 25 more (CURRENT, CHAIN, HOTTEST BLOCK, LIGHT, LED HEAT, BLOCK HEAT, FUSE COOLING, SUPPLY 5 V · LED Vf 2.0 V, BLOCKS ¼ W) and the board legend about 12, so roughly 100 words. DR-40's cap is about 25.

Duplication (DR-41):
- During the play test, "13.6 mA" appears on the monitor tile, again at the end of the LIGHT bar, and again on the panel's Current row (shot 22).
- "220 Ω" and "41 mW" each appear twice.
- The spec "Red LED on 5 V: 12–20 mA" is on both the card and the panel header (shots 13 and 22).
- At the room start, the panel shows the pinball spec before the tray is even fetched. On a phone it sits in the middle of the play view (shot 80).

The monitor's small labels are about 9 px cap height (crop of shot 13), which also fails DR-48.

Toasts print formulas, "(I = (V − Vf) ÷ R)" and "P = I²R" (A8 still open).
findings.verify: Rerun s12-words.mjs: bench total HUD words ≤ 30 and start ≤ 15. In a retaken shot 22, every number appears once on screen. Crop of the meter labels ≥ 14 px cap height.
findings.verify_reason: In my passed-state bench shot, 13.6 mA appears three times: the meter CURRENT tile, the LIGHT bar readout and the panel Current row. 220 Ω appears on the meter and the panel, and 41 mW on the meter and the panel. 'Red LED on 5 V: 12–20 mA' is on both the card and the panel header. Toasts carry formulas, e.g. '(I = (V − Vf) ÷ R)' in shot 28. Meter labels are drawn at 22 px on a 900 px canvas (station.ts:551,557). The meter shows about 390 px wide at 1440×900, so the labels render at about 9.5 px font size, under DR-48's 14 px cap height. I didn't recount words, but card + panel story + rows + toast + prompt plainly exceed the ~25-word DR-40 cap.

findings.title: Grading is untuned: a 0:28 clean run against a 480 s limit, best-of-three makes any finish an A, and tossing a cone counts as damage
findings.problem:
Limits are `{time:480,damage:2,cost:⌈9×1.25⌉=12}` (station.ts:81, :107). The scripted clean solve finished in 0:28 with damage 0 and cost 9: A/A/A (shot 45). A careful human reading every toast finishes well inside 480 s.

Because the overall grade is the best of the three axes (src/sim/grade.ts:6), any finish with time ≤ 480 is an overall A, however many trips and pops there were. The time axis never discriminates.

The damage axis mixes bench mistakes with room props:
- the first thrown cone at t 2.6 already counted damage 1 (s6: "after 1");
- a thrown tray counted damage +1 and cost +10.

So playing with the room (the only chaos available) eats the same 2-point budget as electrical mistakes. Chaos is graded as a mistake, which goes against AGENTS 5 and DR-07.
findings.fix:
1. Set the arcade `limits.time` to 150 s (about 2× a fluent human solve; measure with 3 play-testers).
2. In game.ts:353, for station rooms, grade damage on `station.score().mistakes` only. Report room breakage as a separate fun stat ("Arcade wrecked: 3 props") that never lowers the grade, or give it its own bonus.
3. Show which axis carried the overall on the result card. The time row is already highlighted; add the word 'best'.
findings.verify: Rerun s3-win.mjs: a 0:28 run is A on time. A scripted run at 200 s is B on time. A run that throws 5 props and solves cleanly still has damage 0 on the card.
findings.verify_reason: Partly valid. limits.time is 480 (station.ts:81) against a 0:28 scripted clean run (shot 45), so the time axis never discriminates and, with best-of-three, every finish is an overall A. I confirmed a thrown prop counts damage: my thrown tray gave damage +1 and cost +10 (game.ts:335). But best-of-three is a HARD RULE (AGENTS.md:15, 'Overall grade = best of the three'), and AGENTS.md:14 says destruction is 'allowed and graded'. Counting thrown props as damage is therefore intended Good Job grading, not a violation of AGENTS 5 or DR-07. The real defect is only the untuned time limit (DR-07 wants each axis tuned). I lowered it to P2 because it affects grade meaning, not play.
findings.fix_correction: Drop fix point 2. Room breakage must stay on the damage axis (AGENTS 5/6: destruction is graded, overall = best of three). Excluding it would break the hard rule. Keep point 1: set limits.time to about 150–200 s, after measuring a human solve; the scripted 28 s includes 15 s of soak. Keep point 3: label the axis that carried the grade, which DR-07 asks for. If bench mistakes and room breakage should read differently, show them as two sub-counts on the damage row, both counted.

findings.title: The LED halo and bloom, then a smoke ball, cover the monitor at exactly the moment the player needs to read it (Claw heat and pop)
findings.problem:
Claw with the 220 Ω start, powered:
- The over-rated green LED's halo sprite and point light grow with `glowK` (`ledHalo.scale=.4+glowK*.8`, `ledLight.intensity=glowK*3`, station.ts:408). Under bloom this becomes a soft white disc about 450 px across. It washes out the left half of the meter (CURRENT, LIGHT, LED HEAT) and the chain pads (shot 28).
- 1.2 s later the block pops. A grey smoke burst of 8 particles plus the debris (station.ts:303) forms a solid ball that hides the monitor for about 1 s (shot 29), just as the toast explains the 441 mW.

This breaks DR-66 (glow sprites ≤ 1.5× source, never hide the part being taught) and DR-79 (effects never block more than 0.3 s; no solid smoke balls).
findings.fix:
1. Cap `ledHalo` scale at 0.35 and opacity at 0.5. Set `ledHalo.material.depthTest=true` and render it before the meter (renderOrder −1).
2. Clamp `ledLight.intensity` at 1.2 and set `ledLight.distance` to 0.8 so it doesn't light the monitor.
3. For the white-hot over-rating cue, use dome colour flicker only.
4. In `popBlock`, emit smoke from the board level, drifting away from the camera (+z toward the meter is wrong; use −z velocity), with 4 particles at most and a 0.6 s fade. Delay the toast until the smoke has cleared to 30 % opacity.
findings.verify: Retake shots 28 and 29. Meter text stays legible (contrast ≥ 4.5:1 on the CURRENT tile) in both frames. The smoke covers the monitor for ≤ 0.3 s (shots at +0.1, +0.3, +0.5 s).
findings.verify_reason: In shot 28 a large translucent white wedge covers the lower-left of the meter (labels, LED HEAT and BLOCK HEAT bars) and part of the chain. The values stay readable ('44.8 mA', '220 Ω', '131 °C'), and the CURRENT tile is not washed out, contrary to the claim. In shot 29 a solid grey ball hides the left two-thirds of the meter and part of the board. Code: halo scale .4+glowK*.8 up to about 1.68 m, additive (station.ts:408; kit.ts:66-69). Smoke is 8 puffs, life 1.3–1.9 s, growing ×3.4, opacity up to .5 each (particles.ts:31-33,48-49), so it stacks for well over 0.3 s (DR-79). I lowered it to P2: after the pop the bench is already off and the meter reads POWER OFF/0 Ω, and the explaining toast stays readable on the HUD.
findings.fix_correction: The smoke-direction advice is backwards. The meter stands behind the board, at top-local z −0.56 (station.ts:37), so a −z drift pushes smoke toward the meter and keeps it between camera and meter. Instead, limit the pop to 3–4 puffs with low rise (vy about 0.3) and a short life (≤0.7 s). Cap the opacity at about 0.3 and the growth at ×1.8, and/or drift sideways (±x) away from the meter's centre. Halo: cap the scale at about 0.6 m (≤1.5× source, per DR-66) and the opacity at 0.5. ledLight already has distance 1.6 (station.ts:172); reduce its intensity cap rather than adding a new distance.

findings.title: Bench faults startle nobody: the alarm radius around the bench reaches no coworker, and the kid ignores the sparks
findings.problem:
A trip, a block pop and an LED pop each call `game.alarm({x:table.x,z:table.z},3)` (station.ts:291, :303, :311). The nearest coworkers stand at (5.9,−5.3) and (−6.5,−5.2), 6.5–7 m away (src/levels/arcade.ts:21-24).
- Across all of s2 (2 trips, 1 pop), `snapshot().alarmed` stayed 0.
- The kid only blends between hop and slump (station.ts:428-431); there is no startle on a spark.

The comedy of a 441 mW block popping off lands on an empty room. DR-04 wants a reaction within 0.5 s.
findings.fix:
1. Add two npcs near the bench in src/levels/arcade.ts: a waiting player at (2.6,−0.4) and a technician blob at (−1.6,0.2), both standing.
2. Raise the bench alarm radius to 5 in station.ts.
3. Give the kid a startle: on `trip`, `popBlock` or `popLed`, set `kidBody.position.y+=.25` and arms to −2.8 for 0.4 s.
findings.verify: Rerun s2. `snapshot().alarmed ≥ 1` within 0.5 s of each trip or pop, and the '!' bubble is visible in the bench-view screenshot.
findings.verify_reason: Code check. All three bench faults call game.alarm({table},3) (station.ts:291,303,311). The nearest NPCs are at (5.9,−5.3) and (−6.5,−5.2), 6.55 m and 7.06 m from the table (0,−2.45) (arcade.ts:21-24), so the radius-3 test at game.ts:137 never fires. The kid's pose only blends hop and slump (station.ts:428-431); there is no startle. I didn't rerun the s2 alarmed count, but it follows from the distances.

findings.title: Bench controls break cross-room key meanings and aren't labelled on the parts: E stands up, F flips, 1–4 aren't on the bins, and the POWER lever looks like an arcade joystick
findings.problem:
Key meanings change at the bench (DR-22):
- E (grab/use everywhere else) stands up (game.ts:164). A player pressing E on a hovered bin leaves the bench.
- F (plug everywhere else) flips the LED.

The parts don't show their keys:
- The bins show values, not their 1–4 keys. 1=47, 2=100, 3=220, 4=470 runs across the 2×2 layout (station.ts:194). The prompt "1–4 Take a block" doesn't say which is which.
- The pads show A/S/D and the ACROSS slot shows X, but the lever has no P and no POWER, and the ✓ stamp has no Enter (shot 13).
- In an arcade, the red ball-top lever on a mint box reads as a joystick, not a power switch.

Keyboard-only players have to guess or hover.
findings.verify: Retake shot 13: key chips readable at 1440×900. Test: at the bench, press KeyE while hovering the 220 bin. Expect `held===220` and `atBench` still true.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:164 makes E leave the bench, and the station maps KeyF to flip (station.ts:353), so key meanings differ from DR-22 ('E grab/use, F plug, Esc stand up'). My bench shots show the bins labelled 47/100/220/470 with no 1–4 keys. The 2×2 layout runs 1=47 back-left, 2=100 back-right, 3=220 front-left, 4=470 front-right (station.ts:194). The lever has no P/POWER label and the stamp has no Enter. The lever is a red ball-top stick (station.ts:205), and 'reads like a joystick' is subjective but plausible in an arcade.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-arcade-play-04-retry-P-after-trip.jpg (unlabelled lever and stamp, bins show values only)

findings.title: The card's step 2 ("Step up to the service bench (E)") ticks before step 1 if Pip sits down without the tray, and the card text carries a key hint
findings.fix: In station.ts:110, set `done:()=>(this.active&&this.trayReady)||this.served.length>0` and text 'Step up to the service bench'. Optionally merge steps 1 and 2 into one ('Bring the resistor tray to the service bench').
findings.verify: s4: E at the bench before the tray. The card stays on step 1 with dot 2 grey, and no bell plays.
findings.verify_reason: Reproduced. Sitting at the bench before fetching the tray latched step 2. The dots read 'now,done,,,,,' (step 1 current, step 2 green), and the card flashed 'Step up to the service bench (E)' both at the bench and after Esc. Code: step 2's done is this.active||served.length>0 (station.ts:110), and steps latch (objectives.ts:103). The '(E)' key hint is in the step text.

findings.title: The carry prompt "E  Carry the tray" says the wrong thing: E drops the tray where Pip stands
findings.problem:
While Pip holds the tray more than 2.4 m from the stand, `prompt()` returns `{key:'E',text:'Carry the tray'}` (station.ts:475). E doesn't carry; it puts the tray down on the spot (game.ts:203-212). That is wasted unless the tray is within 2.6 m of the table.

Behind the bench (s10), 1.2 m from the table, the prompt still said "Carry the tray", yet E delivered it. The key prompt doesn't describe its key in either case (DR-19).
findings.fix: In station.ts:475, base the check on the same test as `dropped()`: `const ok=Math.hypot(q.x-t.x,q.z-t.z)<2.6||near<2.2`. Return 'Set the tray on the bench' when ok, else `{key:'E',text:'Put the tray down · Q throws it'}`.
findings.verify: Prompt text checks in a spec: far, 'Put the tray down'; behind the bench within 2.6 m, 'Set the tray on the bench'.
findings.verify_reason: station.ts:475 returns {key:'E',text:'Carry the tray'} when more than 2.4 m from the stand, but E drops the tray (game.ts:206-212), and dropped() only accepts it near the table or stand. Shot 10 shows 'E Carry the tray' mid-hall. I couldn't confirm the reviewer's sub-claim that the prompt read 'Carry' behind the bench. From (0.2,−3.6) the stand is 2.06 m away, so the code would show 'Set the tray on the bench'. The core issue stands.

findings.title: Draw calls 1422 at start and 1497 in survey (R3B measured 1181): a regression against the ≤ 250 budget
findings.problem:
Real-time run at 1440×900 on the host GPU (s11): 60 fps, but `drawCalls` 1422 at start and 1497 in survey. R3B N9 / A13 recorded 1181 and asked for a cut. Clutter (max 220) and 132 props have pushed it up about 20 %.

Lunch went from 1090 to about 175 after `batchProps`. The arcade's dynamic props, bench parts and cabinet sub-meshes aren't merged. On integrated GPUs and phones this will drop frames, which matters doubly since the phone bench already fails.
findings.fix:
1. Merge each static cabinet (room.ts `cabinet()`, called 11×) into one BufferGeometry per material with `mergeGeometries` after building.
2. Merge the bench shell and board static parts (station.ts:137-181) into the decor batch.
3. Instance the bin blocks (4 per bin × 4 bins → `InstancedMesh` per value).
4. Run clutter through the same `batchProps` path Lunch uses.

Target ≤ 300 calls.
findings.verify: Rerun s11-perf.mjs: `drawCalls ≤ 300` at start and survey, fps ≥ 50.
findings.verify_reason: The arcade is over the DR-24 budget: I measured snapshot().drawCalls = 1497 at start and in survey (fullfx). That counter is renderer.info.render.calls across all passes (game.ts:450,504). R3B's 1181 was counted differently (a wrapped drawElements median; R3B noted the old snapshot always said 1), so the '~20 % regression' isn't established. The claim that Lunch dropped to about 175 is contradicted: Lunch measured 1341/1352 with the same metric. Exceeding about 250 is real, but the arcade isn't uniquely bad.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-play/v5-dc.mjs log: 'arcade start dc 1497', 'lunch start dc 1341', 'lunch survey dc 1352'
findings.fix_correction: Drop the Lunch comparison and the 'regression' framing. Report it as a DR-24 budget overrun measured as renderer.info.render.calls with fullfx (arcade 1497, lunch 1341). The suggested merges are fine. Note batchProps already exists (game.ts:139-149); check whether the arcade actually calls it before adding a new path.

findings.title: STOREROOM plaque still floats in mid-air above the storeroom entrance (known DR-72, still open)
findings.problem:
The plaque is a bare PlaneGeometry at (−7.6, 2.1, 2.8) with no mount (room.ts:115). The storeroom walls are only 1.35 m high, so it hangs 0.75 m above them in empty air. It reads clearly as floating at zoom 9 (shots 08, 09) and in the game camera (shots 61, 62, 72).

Orbited, it goes edge-on to a hairline (shot 03). It's also the first world label the player sees on the way to the tray.
findings.fix: Mount the plaque on a frame. Put a plum `rbox(1.6,.46,.06)` on two DMETAL posts `box(.05,.8,.05)` standing on the `store-b` wall top at y 1.35–2.15, with the plane 0.01 m in front of the board. Or lay it on the storeroom wall face at y 1.1 and give it a back so it reads from both sides.
findings.verify: Retake zoom-9 and orbit(±700) shots of the storeroom entrance. Posts touch the wall, and nothing is visible floating.
findings.verify_reason: room.ts:115 places a bare PlaneGeometry at (−7.6, 2.1, 2.8). That x lies in the doorway gap between store-a (ends at x −8.6) and store-b (starts at x −6.55), and the walls are only 1.35 m high (room.ts:76-77). So nothing sits under or behind the plaque. Shot 08 shows it hanging in mid-air over the entrance. This breaks DR-72.

findings.title: Pip walks into coworker blobs: NPCs have no colliders
findings.problem: `addNpc` builds meshes only, with no Rapier body (game.ts:127-134). Walking to (−6.5,−5.8) put Pip inside the sleepy technician blob at (−6.5,−5.2). The blob and Pip's torso interpenetrate (shot 74). Thrown props also pass through coworkers instead of bonking them, which removes a natural slapstick beat and the world reaction (DR-04).
findings.fix: In game.ts addNpc, create a fixed (or kinematic) capsule collider (radius 0.42, half-height 0.3, at y 0.6) per NPC. On contact with a prop moving faster than 3 m/s, call `this.alarm(npc.position,1.5)` and add a wobble.
findings.verify: Walk Pip into each arcade NPC: Pip stops at a centre distance ≥ 0.74 m. Throw a crate at a blob: `alarmed ≥ 1` within 0.5 s.
findings.verify_reason: addNpc only builds meshes and creates no Rapier body (game.ts:127-134). I walked Pip at the sleepy blob (−6.5,−5.2) and he arrived at (−6.42,−5.14), 0.1 m from its centre, inside it.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/tools/verify-arcade-play/v4-flow.mjs log: '#18 walk into npc {x:-6.42,z:-5.14} arrived true'

findings.title: Space at the bench makes Pip jump into the bench camera (white mitts pop into frame)
findings.problem: Space isn't a station key, so it falls through to `action('jump')` (game.ts:164-166, :182) while seated. Pip rises to y 2.0 and his mitts appear at the bottom centre of the bench view (shot 55). It's harmless but looks like a glitch, and is another example of walking keys leaking into the bench.
findings.fix: Same fix as the R finding: at the bench, return after `station.key()` for every key (game.ts:164). Optionally map Space to `signoff` or `power` for a big-button feel.
findings.verify: At the bench press Space: `snapshot().player.y` stays 0.77 and the bench shot is clean.
findings.verify_reason: Space at the bench raised the player from y 0.77 to 1.92. White mitts pop up at the bottom centre of the bench frame (my shot 06, reviewer shot 55). Space isn't in the station map, so it falls through to action('jump') (game.ts:164,166,181).

findings.title: The serviced cabinet's ribbon cable ends on the bench top short of the board, so the link between cabinet and channel board isn't shown
findings.problem:
The GRAPE tube from the serviced cabinet (station.ts:222-223) ends at cabinet-local (1.8,1.05,0.5). In world space that is about (−1.09,1.05,−3.0), behind the bins and about 0.5 m from the board's SUPPLY terminal at about (−0.98,−2.49).

In the bench view it's a short lilac stub lying loose on the bench (shot 13, upper left of the bins). It reads as a stray pen. The one physical cable in the room doesn't visibly carry the cabinet's LED channel onto the board, though that is exactly what the board represents.
findings.fix: Extend the CatmullRom points so the tube runs down off the cabinet, along the bench back edge, and into a connector block at the board's left edge next to SUPPLY. Board-local is (SUPX−.15, TOPZ); convert with `this.top.localToWorld`. Add a plug box `rbox(.12,.06,.1)` there. When live, run Lunch-style `Pulses` along it (current flowing), which also gives the room a visible cable (DR-05/DR-46).
findings.verify: Retake the bench view: the ribbon ends in a connector at the SUPPLY terminal, and on a live circuit pulses move along it.
findings.verify_reason: I computed the tube's end. Cabinet-local (1.8,1.05,0.5), with the group at (−2.95,0,−2.8) and ry 0.38, ends at world ≈(−1.09,1.05,−3.0). The board's SUPPLY terminal is at ≈(−0.98,−2.49), about 0.52 m away. In the bench shots it reads as a loose lilac stub, like a pen, upper-left of the bins (my shots 04/05).

findings.title: Inside the storeroom the 1.35 m half-wall hides Pip's body at low or side orbits and doesn't fade
findings.problem:
The storeroom walls `store-a` and `store-b` are interior walls 1.35 m high (room.ts:76-77). With Pip at the tray counter and the camera orbited toward the hall (shot 76), only Pip's hat and shoulders show above the wall; the legs and the held tray are hidden.

The occlusion fade only applies to `this.occluders` (game.ts:386-388), which doesn't fade this wall. DR-12 wants meshes over 1.2 m between the camera and Pip to fade to ≤ 0.25 opacity.
findings.fix: Register the storeroom interior walls as occluders (push their meshes into `game.occluders` from `kit.interiorWall`). Or drop them to 1.0 m (below Pip's chest) and cap them with the wood rail, which keeps the storeroom read.
findings.verify: Retake shot 76: at least 70 % of Pip's pixels are visible, and the wall is at opacity ≤ 0.25 when between the camera and Pip.
findings.verify_reason: Shot 76 is real: only Pip's hat and shoulders show above the store-a wall, and the wall isn't faded. But the cause is misdiagnosed. interiorWall already pushes every wall mesh into game.occluders (src/levels/decor.ts:44-49, with the comment 'Interior walls fade like pillars'). The wall doesn't fade because the fade test casts a single ray to p.y+.4 (game.ts:387). From a high camera that ray passes over the 1.35 m wall top, even though the wall hides Pip's legs and torso. This is the known DR-12 issue.
findings.fix_correction: Don't register the walls again; they are already occluders. Cast three rays (feet at about p.y−.6, chest at p.y+.2, head at p.y+.7) in game.ts:387, fade any occluder that any of them hits, and fade to ≤0.25 opacity instead of .15 (already fine). Alternatively lower the storeroom walls to about 1.0 m.

findings.title: The tray is carried tilted beside Pip, not level in front of the chest
findings.problem:
In the game-camera carry shot (shot 10) the pink tray hangs diagonally off Pip's right side, with the blocks tilted. At zoom 9 (shot 09) it floats beside Pip's head, offset to the left.

The carry target puts the prop 1.05 m ahead at chest height but zeroes only angular velocity (game.ts:331). The tray keeps whatever tilt it had at pickup, and the blocks riding on it copy that rotation (station.ts:369). This breaks DR-65.
findings.fix: In game.ts:331, for light held props, also slerp the body rotation toward yaw=heading with pitch/roll 0 (`b.setRotation(q.slerp(target,.3))`). Reduce `ahead` to 0.7 for the tray, so it sits between the mitts.
findings.verify: Crop the carry pose at zoom 9: the tray's top face is within 5° of level and centred on Pip's chest. The bounding box doesn't intersect a 0.3 m sphere at head height.
findings.verify_reason: The carry code sets linvel toward a point 1.05 m ahead at p.y+.55 and only zeroes angvel (game.ts:331), so the pickup tilt persists. trayRide copies the body rotation (station.ts:369). In shot 10 the tray hangs diagonally at Pip's right side. This breaks DR-65.

notes.fun:
What works:
- Popping a block is the best moment in the room: a crack, candy debris and a puff of smoke, and the bench cuts out.
- The tripped PTC fuse glows red and visibly cools back to yellow; it reads well and it's physical.
- The candy block colours and the big ✓ stamp give the bench a pleasant toy feel.
- Signing off rings a bell and lights a back-wall cabinet, which you can see from the room camera.

What doesn't:
- The room is a long hallway to a keypad. Fetching the tray takes about 8 s at sprint. After that, about 95 % of play happens in a fixed bench camera that can't be orbited or zoomed.
- The things that should be funny are all off-screen at the bench: the kid hopping or slumping, the TILT! marquee, the serviced cabinet's lamp, and the back-wall cabinets lighting up.
- Nobody in the room reacts to the trips and pops; `alarmed` stayed 0.
- There is no cable, no designed chaos route and no physical bonus. Throwing the tray at the bench is not accepted, and chaos in the room (tossing a cone) costs grade.
- Cabinets 3–5 share one answer (470 + 470 Ω), so the last two jobs are repeats.
- Overall the arcade is pleasant but not a Good Job-style comedy room. The best fixes are to bring the payoff into frame, accept a thrown tray, and add one cable or chaos act in the hall.
notes.playability:
On desktop the clean route is solid:
- The clutter lanes keep the storeroom run and the bench approach clear, with no stall in any of my walks.
- The tray is reachable, and it can be recovered from behind the bench via the right end.
- Dropping the tray from behind the bench counts.
- The audit shows 0 overlaps, there were no console errors in any of the 14 runs, and the frame rate held at 60 fps (but with 1422 draw calls).
- Fuse cool-down is 2.5 s and the play test is 3 s, so there is no dead wait over 3 s.

Blocking problems:
1. Phone portrait can't finish the job (P0). The sign-off stamp and two bins are off-screen and the bench has no touch buttons. In landscape the HUD covers the lever and the stamp.
2. P is a toggle while its prompt reads 'Fuse cooling' or 'Play test'. The natural retry turns the bench off, which is exactly the DR-19 failure.
3. R at the bench reloads the level without a confirm.
4. Space, Tab and Q also leak through at the bench.
5. The prompts invite graded mistakes: 'P Power on' appears on three cabinets that start broken.
6. Brute force is free: the meter is live, swaps under 0.6 s are never counted, and parts are billed only at sign-off.
7. Smaller issues: Pip walks through coworkers; the storeroom half-wall hides Pip; a thrown tray doesn't count.
notes.clarity:
Good:
- The start view is readable. The tray glows on a dark counter in a clearly signed storeroom, and the marker cone points at it.
- The bench parts are legible: the value-coloured bins, the A/S/D/X pads printed on the board, and the reversed-LED '+' marker moving.
- The LIGHT bar's band and ★ zone are a clear target.

Weak:
- While carrying, the marker follows the tray in Pip's hands, not the bench.
- The bench shows about 100 words with values repeated three times. The monitor labels are about 9 px.
- At the start, the panel shows the pinball spec before it matters, and covers the middle of a phone screen.
- Keys aren't on the parts: no 1–4 on the bins, no P or POWER on a lever that looks like an arcade joystick, no Enter on the stamp.
- E means 'stand up' and F means 'flip' at the bench, against their meanings elsewhere.
- The card's step 2 ticks out of order if you sit before fetching the tray.
- Prompts describe states ('Fuse cooling') rather than what the key does.
- The LED halo, then a smoke ball, hide the monitor at the Claw failure, exactly when the player needs to read it.
notes.teaching:
The underlying model is truthful and well commented (logic.ts:1-17). The PTC self-reset, 'over-rating runs hot and dies early', series-adds and parallel-shares, the across-the-LED trap and polarity are all acted out with physical blocks, which is a real improvement on R4's rack menu.

The teaching is undercut in three ways:
1. The live meter plus free fast swaps let players tune by watching the bar rather than predicting with I = (V − Vf) ÷ R.
2. Cabinets 3–5 have the same 940 Ω answer, so battery life and base current don't change what the player does.
3. The toasts and story print the formula and part of the answer ('Only 0.3 V is left over…', '(I = (V − Vf) ÷ R)'), against 'say why, never how' (A8 still open).

Powering the start state just to look is counted as a mistake. That punishes the diagnostic habit the room should encourage (A7 still open).
notes.models:
(Not this reviewer's main dimension; noted while playing.)
- The bench, bins, candy blocks with real colour bands, PTC disc, LED with a cathode flat, and the TO-92 and coin-wheel motor are detailed enough at the bench camera.
- The back-wall cabinets have distinct props on each one (pinball table, dance pad, claw box, handheld, hopper) and finished backs (shot 75).
- The play-test kid is still a realistic human child (DR-60, shots 41 and 72).
- The STOREROOM plaque floats in mid-air.
- The cabinet ribbon cable ends loose on the bench.
- The tray is carried tilted.
- The pastel clutter (pink and teal crates, macaron-like beanbags) and the confetti carpet stay busy at the game camera (shots 01 and 02), but the bench still reads as the focal point in the survey.

rechecked: A2 PTC fuse self-resets: FIXED. It glows red, counts down 'FUSE COOLING 2.4 s' and conducts again by itself (shot 20).
A3 LED slightly over rating no longer dies: FIXED. 44.8 mA (2.24×) gives 'runs hot and dies early' and no LED pop (shot 28).
A4 soak: PARTIAL. The play test is 3 s × 5, but the kid it depends on is off-camera at the bench, so it plays as 3 s of progress bar.
A5 hotkeys and side panel: STILL OPEN. 12 bench keys, the panel still repeats the monitor's values, and the keys aren't labelled on the bins, lever or stamp.
A6 R4B redesign (ricochet pops, kid queue, feed-cable pulses, giant LED): NOT BUILT, confirmed.
A7 experiments graded as damage: STILL OPEN, and the prompts now actively invite it ('P Power on' on the broken rhythm, claw and handheld starts).
A8 messages say why, never the fix: STILL OPEN. The toasts print '(I = (V − Vf) ÷ R)' and 'P = I²R', and the Rhythm story gives the 0.3 V hint.
A9 confetti carpet: FIXED to dusty mauve, but the scatter still reads busy at the game camera (shots 01, 02).
A10 confetti through the bench camera: FIXED. No confetti over the monitor after sign-off (shots 24, 26).
A11 stale toast after sitting: FIXED on sitting. A toast still persists for about 4 s after standing up (s4 'esc'), which is minor.
A12 phone bench layout: STILL OPEN and now a P0. The sign-off stamp and the 47/220 bins are off-screen in portrait, and the HUD covers them in landscape.
A13 draw calls: REGRESSION. 1181 (R3B) → 1422 at start and 1497 in survey (s11, real time, 60 fps on the host GPU).
DR-19 arcade check (power, trip, fix, P): FAIL. The run ends POWER OFF (shot 52).
DR-60 arcade kid: STILL OPEN. A realistic human child with a skin-tone head (shots 41, 72).
DR-72 floating STOREROOM sign: STILL OPEN (shots 08, 09, 62).
DR-41 duplicate values: STILL OPEN. The spec appears on both the card and the panel, and 13.6 mA appears three times (shot 22).
DR-48 meter label size: STILL OPEN. About 9 px caps (crop of shot 13).
DR-70 start overlaps: PASS. `g.audit(.02)` returned [] at start.
DR-80: PASS. `g.close()` returned [] for every arcade-play script (s1–s13).
